stories.headline: Odisha govt orders evacuation as fresh cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal
stories.title: Odisha govt orders evacuation as fresh cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal
stories.summary: Odisha govt orders evacuation as fresh cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government has ordered the evacuation of people living in low-lying areas and hilly terrain as a fresh cyclone developing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on 3 November, officials said.

The state administration has stepped up preparedness measures, particularly in southern districts, which are still dealing with the impact of cyclone 'Arnab' that triggered heavy rainfall and flooding in Ganjam and Gajapati districts.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified into a deep depression early Sunday and was likely to develop into a cyclonic storm within the next six hours.
The weather system is expected to intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by 2 November.

The IMD said the system is very likely to move west-northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur by the morning of 3 November, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 100-110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph.
Under its influence, southern Odisha is likely to experience light to moderate rainfall at many places, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on 3 and 4 November.
The Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar has issued a warning for southern Odisha districts for 2 and 3 November, forecasting rainfall between 7 cm and 20 cm.
These areas were already affected by cyclone 'Arnab', which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast on 28 October.
The IMD has also warned of strong winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, from the evening of 2 November.
Wind speeds may increase to 50-60 kmph, with gusts reaching 70 kmph, on 3 November before gradually weakening the following day.

Reviewing the preparedness measures, Odisha Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari chaired a meeting on Saturday to assess arrangements for evacuation, relief and rescue operations in view of the potential cyclone and heavy rainfall.
The Ganjam district administration has directed officials to ensure adequate stocks of food, drinking water and other essential supplies in areas vulnerable to flooding and waterlogging.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab aftermath: Flood-hit villages in Odisha face drinking water crisis
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab aftermath: Flood-hit villages in Odisha face drinking water crisis
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: An acute shortage of safe drinking water has compounded the suffering of thousands of people affected by floods in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts of southern Odisha.
Days of inundation caused by cyclone Arnab have left families struggling to access food, clean water, sanitation facilities and medical assistance.
With hand pumps submerged in stagnant floodwater, residents say that the few functioning tube wells are supplying potentially contaminated water, raising fears of outbreaks of water-borne diseases.
“The biggest problem is drinking water.
Rescue boats are the only means of reaching the main road,” said Santi Behera, 43, of Rajapur village in Ganjam district.
Balabhadra Sahoo, 55, of Biripur village in the same district, said his family had lost its home and crops in the floods and was now struggling to obtain drinking water.
Ranjan Sahoo, 63, of Badamadhapur village in Chatrapur block, Ganjam district, said polluted floodwater had left villagers with little choice but to avoid cooked meals.

Meanwhile, the Housing and Urban Development Department has deployed teams from the Water Corporation of Odisha (WATCO) and the Public Health Engineering Organisation (PHEO) to oversee drinking-water supplies and sanitation arrangements in flood-affected areas.
All water sources, including community water facilities, are to be cleaned and disinfected.

Post-flood sanitation and the restoration of hygienic conditions are also being prioritised, said Anisha Kar, public relations officer with the Information and Public Relations Department of the Odisha government.
Suresh Pujari, the revenue and disaster management minister, said the department was prepared to provide assistance to flood victims.
Four helicopters were being used to transport food packets to isolated areas, with airdrops planned at 21 identified locations.

stories.headline: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
stories.title: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
stories.summary: It comes amid growing protests over a voter roll revision exercise feared to leave 130 million voters off rolls.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tens of thousands of people have gathered in Delhi for a major opposition rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner and electoral reforms.

The rally, organised by the main opposition Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, is taking place at Ramlila Maidan, a large ground in central Delhi known for hosting political rallies and protests.
Visuals showed Gandhi in an open-top jeep alongside other opposition leaders heading towards the venue.
The Gen Z-led pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has also pledged support, though its leaders have yet to be seen.
Security has been tightened, with thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed near the grounds.
Sunday's event is the latest show of opposition anger over a voter-list revision exercise that has removed 130 million names from draft electoral rolls in India.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) says the exercise is aimed at updating the voters' list by purging names of people who have died or moved away from their registered addresses.

But opposition parties allege that the exercise - known as the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) - could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing eligible voters from the rolls.
They accuse the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the BJP of "vote chori (theft)".
Both the BJP and the ECI have denied the allegations.

The controversy intensified in September when The Indian Express newspaper in its investigation, external reported that the CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, made key decisions related to the exercise without the agreement of the two other election commissioners, who had raised objections on more than a dozen occasions.
The Election Commission said differences of opinion were normal in any institution and did not affect its functioning.

stories.headline: INDIA bloc leaders pass motion seeking impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: INDIA bloc leaders pass motion seeking impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 31: The Congress-led INDIA bloc on Saturday held a mock ‘public impeachment’ of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence, accusing him of electoral malpractice and demanding his removal. Kharge moved a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar’s removal, alleging that he had acted against the interests of democracy. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, other Opposition MPs, jurists, lawyers and civil society members attended the meeting, which was presided over by former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar. Kharge listed six charges against the CEC, including conspiring to steal elections, deleting 13.2 crore voters from electoral rolls, rewriting Form 6 applications, and taking control of electoral rolls through ECINET. The Opposition also accused Gyanesh Kumar of ignoring the views of the other two Election Commissioners and working at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would not continue in office, claiming that the Opposition had enough evidence to ensure his removal. ANI meanwhile reports that INDIA bloc leaders passed a motion seeking the impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar during a symbolic public impeachment programme organised against him. The event was held to register the opposition bloc’s protest against the CEC. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor, according to PTI described the INDIA bloc’s ‘Mock Parliament’, held at party president Mallikarjun Kharge’s residence in Delhi, as a dignified and constructive discussion reflecting a strong commitment to protecting Indian democracy. Following the meeting, Tharoor said the same spirit would carry forward to the bloc’s Maha Rally at Ramlila Maidan, where lakhs of people are expected to participate tomorrow. The meeting was organised after authorities denied permission for holding it at Ramlila Maidan. The INDIA bloc raised three key demands: restoration of names of voters allegedly removed from electoral rolls, removal of the CEC and repeal of the law granting immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner. The Opposition is also scheduled to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 as part of its ‘vote chori’ campaign against the Election Commission and the Centre.

stories.headline: Supreme Court paves way for IT assessments of two businessmen sons of former CJI Y.K. Sabharwal
stories.title: Supreme Court paves way for IT assessments of two businessmen sons of former CJI Y.K. Sabharwal
stories.summary: A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, while upholding income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has cleared the decks for the income-tax assessments of the two businessmen sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal over share transactions that funded their purchase of a prime property on Delhi's Sikandra Road in 2010.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by Chetan and Nitin Sabharwal, while upholding income tax reassessment notices issued for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10.

Justice Sabharwal served as the 36th Chief Justice of India (November 1, 2005 to January 14, 2007) and had a long judicial career spanning the Delhi High Court, Bombay High Court, and the Supreme Court of India.
The top court said the notice issued by the Income Tax Department dated March 31, 2015, rested on valid "reason to believe" under Sections 147 and 148 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

The apex court, in its October 28 judgment, said the probe report by the director general provided tangible material for the Assessing Officer to form a reasonable belief that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment.
It said "reason to believe" means cause or justification, and the officer need not have finally proved the escape of income.
It said Courts cannot weigh the sufficiency of the reasons and rejected the argument that overvaluation cannot lead to escaped income.

"The escapement of income at the hands of the seller of the shares, the proceeds of which were later utilised to acquire capital assets to thus claim deduction, could as well be a diversion of income, assessable to tax under the guise of sale proceeds which, in the present case, assumes relevance for reason of the sale proceeds being far above the actual value of the shares....
"The present case is not one wherein it could be said that the Assessing Officer had only a vague feeling on the basis of which he recorded that proper investigation was necessary.

We are of the view that a conclusion that the truth of the alleged transactions needs to be investigated is not the same thing as having reasons, post investigation, to issue a notice," the bench said.
In October 2007, the Sabharwal brothers and two other shareholders agreed to sell shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd to GYS Real Estate Pvt Ltd.
The agreed prices were Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, with each seller entitled to a one-fourth share.

stories.headline: 6 Indian tourists go missing during trek to deepest lake of Nepal, Shey-Phoksundo
stories.title: 6 Indian tourists go missing during trek to deepest lake of Nepal, Shey-Phoksundo
stories.summary: Kathmandu , November 1 : Six Indian tourists have gone missing during a trek to Shey-Phoksundo Lake, the deepest lake of Nepal, after heavy snowfall in the area, officials confirmed. The India tourists, who include two women and four men, are confirmed to have gone missing while travelling from Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Dolpo Buddha Rural Municipality towards Shey-Phoksundo Lake. They were last reported missing in the Numla Pass and Bagla Pass areas between Ward Nos. 4 and 8 of Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality. Local guides suspect that the tourists may have become stranded following heavy snowfall in the Himalayan region, reportedly influenced by Cyclone Arnab developing in the Bay of Bengal. According to local officials, the tourists proceeded towards the high-altitude area despite warnings from residents that crossing the mountain passes would be difficult due to snowfall. They are believed to have become trapped in the snow while returning. Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Hamal confirmed that “the tourists became stranded while returning from Dho towards Phoksundo Lake.” She said, “They had been warned by locals about the difficult weather and mountain conditions but proceeded with their journey.” Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality Chairman Dhawa Samduk Gurung said, “Mobile phone communication is unavailable in the mountain passes between Wards 4 and 8, making it difficult to obtain information about the tourists’ whereabouts and current condition.” According to the District Administration Office, “A total of 244 tourists have reached Upper Dolpa. Of them, 149 are Nepali nationals, 44 are from SAARC countries, and 51 are citizens of other foreign countries.” In view of the adverse weather conditions, the district administration has urged tourists to avoid risky areas and remain in safe locations. Tourist arrivals in the Shey-Phoksundo Lake area have been increasing in recent years. According to available data, 4,882 tourists visited Phoksundo Lake during the first 11 months of the fiscal year 2082/83. Dolpa Deputy Superintendent of Police Anil Raj Giri said, “Six Indian tourists remain out of contact, according to the latest information.” Further adding, “Authorities have requested the concerned agency to arrange a helicopter for search and rescue operations.” Search and rescue efforts have been hampered by heavy snowfall and adverse weather conditions in the high Himalayan region. The absence of mobile phone connectivity in the area and thick snow have made it difficult to determine the tourists’ whereabouts and condition. A team of the Nepal Army has also been deployed to locate the tourists and assist in their rescue. (ANI)
